target_customer: Large enterprise procurement, finance and IT teams that buy software and services
problem: Employees buy outside procurement rules because purchase intake is slow and fragmented; Zip gives a single intake and approval flow that routes requests to the right reviewers and systems.
business_model: Enterprise SaaS subscription for intake to pay procurement, plus payments add ons

founders.name: Lu Cheng
prior_employers: Airbnb (six years, most recently Head of Engineering for Airbnb Experiences)
founders.background_notes: Per YC page. TechCrunch calls both founders former Airbnb engineers and says they founded Zip in July 2020.

competitors.name: Coupa Software
competitors.what: Public spend management and procurement suite
competitors.traction_then: Fiscal 2020 (year ended January 2020) revenue of 389.7M, up 50 percent; 753 customers above 100K annual subscription as of October 2019

technical_complexity.rationale: Workflow engine and many enterprise integrations (ERP, finance, security tools) built by a small team; hard part was integrations and enterprise security rather than novel research.

defensibility.rationale: Once embedded in approval workflows and integrated with ERP and finance systems it is costly to replace, but competing suites could add intake features.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: A May 2026 item notes Coupa launched a competing agent orchestration product, while Zip kept winning customers and raised through 2024.

market_need_then: Pandemic era software and vendor sprawl; large procurement suites were seen as heavy and slow to adopt while employees bought outside the process. Hard demand figures from 2020 were not found.

branding.name_origin: Not explained in sources. CB Insights lists the company as formerly Evergreen; the date and reason for the rename were not found.
branding.domain_note: Originally ziphq.com; the site now redirects to zip.com (seen 2026). Zip Co (zip.co, a buy now pay later firm) is an unrelated company with the same name.

identity.logo: Letter Z with a graph line running through it, from the October 2024 rebrand
identity.visual_style: Flow and Peak themes with fluid motion design; brand built with CoLab agency
identity.voice_and_tone: Confident, optimistic and enterprise focused, leaning on headline metrics

branding.brand_signature: The Z with a rising line and the Flow and Peak motion language

rebrands.to: New Flow and Peak identity with Z mark
rebrands.why: Zip began as an intake tool and grew into an AI platform covering all spend, so the brand needed to reflect that expansion (Zip brand story, October 28, 2024)

branding.community_and_virality: Fast Company Innovation by Design recognition in 2025 and an SF Design Week award listing for the rebrand; no community or merch found.

brand_strength.rationale: Strong enterprise brand with design awards and big logos, but a generic, confusable name shared with an unrelated payments company, and no evidence the brand drove growth.

outcome_analysis: Zip is one of the strongest Summer 2020 companies: an 11.1M seed in August 2020, a 43M Series B at 1.2B in May 2022, 100M at 1.5B in 2023 and 190M at 2.2B in October 2024 led by BOND, with a team around 500 and large enterprise logos. Founders with Airbnb engineering and YC partner experience, plus an intake first wedge that avoided head on replacement of Coupa and Ariba, drove growth. No failure signals were found.
notes: A Series A of about 25M to 27M (Seedtable dates it August 2021) appears in aggregator summaries but the article was not opened and the amount conflicts, so it is not recorded as a round; total raised stated at 181M after the Series C by TechCrunch and Crunchbase News and about 371M after the Series D by aggregators. Seed investors come from a Seedtable listing only (CRV lead, YC participating). Founder education was not found. TechCrunch (2023) names Keelvar and Focal Point as competitors and Crunchbase News (2023) names SAP, Ariba and Coupa as incumbents; those are dated 2023 so only Coupa's 2020 filing is used. Series B stage label was cited by Sacra and Pulse 2.0; Team Blind labels Zip a Series D company, which fits the 2024 round.
